messages:
Nina (oncall): seeing a sustained p99 jump in chicago-pop starting ~02:17 UTC. Throughput down ~30% on /v1/generate. Any recent rollouts? :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy finished by Cassie at 02:12 UTC — runtime: kernel-selector v2.3.1 rolled to chicago-pop
Cassie (eng-runtime): does that match the timeframe. I'll pull selector + kvcache metrics now
Mike (eng-sre): network quick check — no interface down, but noticing an AS-path change through EdgeHub provider around 02:16:55, added ~12ms and jitter for a subset of nodes
Rajiv (eng-runtime): grabbed a few traces. Kernel selector is oscillating between fast_mha and fallback_q4 every few dozen requests. Batch size is jumping 1->4 dynamically. That combo is thrashing the KV cache keys (compiled-kernel + batch tuple).
Rajiv (eng-runtime): ```
[02:17:24] kernel_choice: fast_mha (score=0.62)
[02:17:24] kernel_choice: fallback_q4 (score=0.61)
KVCache stats (chicago-pop node-7): hits=31%, misses=69%, evictions=88k/min
Profile sample: self_time spike in kernel_switch path and serialize_kvcache()
```
Yun (ml-eng): did the seq_len distribution change? evictions suggest bigger contexts or more churn
Cassie (eng-runtime): seq_len p50 ~512 as usual but tail (p95->p99) moved to ~2048 because a small customer batch increased long-history requests. Selector's "aggressive-batch" logic tried to increase batch to recover throughput and kept switching kernels when network jitter changed RTTs.
Nina (oncall): is that heuristic new in v2.3.1?
Cassie (eng-runtime): yes — v2.3.1 added an "aggressive-batch" fallback with weak hysteresis. It interprets transient latency as spare capacity and ups batch, which then changes which kernel is optimal. With the altered AS path jitter that became a feedback loop.
Mike (eng-sre): summary: provider routing change -> increased jitter -> selector misinterprets -> kernel/batch oscillation -> KV cache thrash -> p99 + throughput regression.
Rajiv (eng-runtime): short mitigation: pin kernel-selector to stable v2.2.5 and disable aggressive-batch in chicago-pop, plus restart the KV cache process on the worst nodes to reclaim memory. Applying patch to 4 affected nodes now.
Cassie (eng-runtime): rolling patch to node pool alpha-chi-1 (4 nodes) — disabling aggressive-batch and forcing selector v2.2.5 override.
deploy-bot: patch rollout started (0/4) at 02:29 UTC
Cassie (eng-runtime): patch applied to 4/4 at 02:31 UTC
Nina (oncall): monitoring — p99 falling back to baseline, KV hit-rate recovering. At 02:40 UTC p99 back to normal and hit-rate ~90% on nodes we patched. Throughput recovered to ~98% of baseline. :white_check_mark:
Yun (ml-eng): follow-ups: (1) add robust hysteresis to batching heuristic (2) make kernel-selector resilient to transient RTT variance (3) alert on KV eviction rate > 20k/min and automatic soft-pin to stable selector version
Rajiv (eng-runtime): I uploaded flamegraphs + sample traces to s3://redwood-internal/chicago/1782304123/ and I'll open a post-incident PR with metrics and a reproducible harness for selector oscillation.
Cassie (eng-runtime): opening a ticket now with links to logs, PR, and rollout notes. Tagging networking and provider contacts for EdgeHub routing change.
Mike (eng-sre): recommend we also request BGP history from EdgeHub for 02:15-02:20 UTC to correlate.
Nina (oncall): agreed — assigning follow-ups and closing incident once PR lands and alert rules are in place. Thanks all for quick response.
